Subject: Redwood connector — initial requirements and test scope

Hi Diego,

Thanks again for taking this on. I attached our initial requirements doc (clutch-requirements-v1.pdf) — the ask from our platform team is simple: validate the connector reference design for production-readiness and exercise fallback behaviors when the primary Redwood model variant is under load.

Wanted to surface a few specifics up front so your validation plan can include them:
- Multi-tenant routing: our tenants use both short (<=128) and long (>=2048) contexts; we need representative latency/throughput numbers for both.
- Failure modes: graceful degradation to a smaller model variant or cached response; measurable error budgets for 99th/95th percentiles.
- Security: tokenization and PII redaction in transit + compliance evidence pointers.
- Canary policy: we'd like to see a canary that starts at 1% traffic, ramps to 20% over 24h with automatic rollback on quality regression.

Can you confirm your proposed validation steps and a rough schedule? We can provide staging credentials and sample payloads once you confirm scope.

—Anne-Marie

Anne-Marie — thanks for the clear brief and the doc. Looping in Lauren (partner ops) and Karthik + Sergio from platform/serving so we can align on the technical validation. Below is our proposed approach; please call out anything missing.

Proposed validation plan (high level):
1) Reference-design sanity checks (2 days)
   - Validate auth flow, request/response schema, header propagation, and throttling behavior.
   - Verify network path and TLS mutual-auth if requested.
2) Workload matrix tests (3 days)
   - Short context throughput profile (<=128): sustained 200 RPS target over N parallel clients.
   - Long context latency profile (>=2048): tail-latency SLOs measured at 95/99.
3) Failover & fallback matrix (2 days)
   - Induce replica loss / model-variant OOM and assert automatic fallback to quantized variant or cached prefix response.
   - Assert per-tenant isolation under noisy neighbors.
4) Canary + rollback exercise (1 day)
   - Execute a canary ramp (1% -> 20% over 24h) in our staging cluster; validate automatic rollback triggers (latency regressions, token-level mismatches).
5) Security/compliance verification (1 day)
   - Confirm data-in-transit encryption, KMS integration, and provide checklist items for SOC2 evidence.

Artifacts we'll produce: connector-checklist workbook (attached), a test harness repo link, and a short runbook documenting observed fallbacks and mitigation steps.

Open items for you:
- Provide staging endpoint and credentials (or an allowlisted IP range).
- Sample payloads and a small labeled prompt set for quality checks.
- Any regulatory constraints around logging or token retention we should be aware of.

Proposed target: start the validation next Wednesday (2027-04-07) and complete the run in the following 8 business days. Let us know if you prefer an earlier start.

Thanks — Diego

Anne-Marie / team — quick technical notes from serving/runtime perspective to make sure the validation covers the tricky edge cases: 

1) Batching and latency floors: when we exercise high-RPS short-context workloads, we'll measure per-request queuing and ensure batching gains don't push the 50th/95th under your thresholds. If you want deterministic latency you can opt-in to smaller batching windows at the cost of throughput.

2) KV cache invalidation: for long-context summarization, we recommend a KV-cache sweep step in the harness to reproduce cache-warm vs cache-cold behavior; that often explains 99th percentile spikes.

3) Model-variant fallbacks: we'll validate two fallback paths — (a) automatic quantized variant (reduced-context precision) and (b) cached prefix-only responses. For each, we'll verify the fallback signal (reason codes) appear in the trace so you can attribute quality regressions.

4) Canary rollback triggers: suggest we monitor three signals and trigger rollback on any one: (i) 10%+ drop in semantic-match score on the labeled prompt set, (ii) 200ms+ increase in P50 latency, (iii) lambda error rate > 1%. We can tune thresholds during the first hour of the canary.

Ask: could you share a representative 10-line sample payload (one short, one long) so we can sanity-check serialization, headers, and size limits?

I'll assemble the test harness tasks into Jira tasks and assign owners.

—Karthik
